proof_summary: The block \([2,4,2,4,2]\), occurring in \(5,7,11,13,17,19\), has offsets \(0,2,6,8,12,14\), which cover every residue class modulo \(5\). Thus any occurrence would contain a prime divisible by \(5\), forcing that prime to be \(5\); consequently its starting index is at most \(3\), so the block has only finitely many occurrences.
